source.title: Practical Assessment of Generalization Performance Robustness for Deep Networks via Contrastive Examples
source.authors: Xuanyu Wu; Xu-Hong Li; Haoyi Xiong; Xiao Zhang; Siyu Huang; D. Dou

record.tranche_reason: Measures whether accuracy and feature Fisher ratios on transformed training examples track test accuracy across datasets and model settings, using a different method from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates generalization estimates from contrastive examples and feature Fisher ratios. It does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or example removal.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates its own generalization estimator, ContRE. It invokes memorization as motivation and compares against a sharpness baseline, but reports no results establishing or contradicting V1–V8. Correlations between transformed-image accuracy or Fisher ratios and test accuracy do not test magnitude-aware weight sharpness, architecture advantages, or the specified training interventions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that accuracy and feature Fisher ratios on ContRE examples estimate relative generalization performance across the tested image-classification settings. They also report generalization-gap prediction when training accuracy is comparable, while warning about unsuitable transformations, missing theoretical links, and extension beyond images.
record.recipe_differences: Uses randomized image transformations on training samples and measures accuracy or feature Fisher ratio against test accuracy; the versions describe other interventions and measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Correlations vary by dataset and transformation; the authors report dataset-dependent performance for individual transformations and reduced partial correlation on ImageNet. RandAugment-trained models show higher Random Flip and Random Rotation correlations than ContRE.

fits_no_version.finding: ContRE accuracy correlates with test accuracy at 0.965, 0.974, and 0.970 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Accuracy on randomized transformations of training images can rank relative test accuracy across image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimator correlations depend on transformation, dataset, training augmentation, and available training data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The usefulness of transformed-training-image accuracy as a generalization estimator depends on evaluation and training conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: ContRE retains partial correlations of 0.938, 0.962, and 0.774 after controlling for training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ContRE accuracy remains associated with test accuracy after controlling for training accuracy, with dataset-dependent strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature Fisher ratios correlate with test accuracy across datasets and hyperparameter choices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class separation of features from transformed training images is associated with held-out classification accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 4 reports generalization-gap prediction scores of 13.531 for ContRE and 10.667 for an unspecified sharpness baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ContRE outperforms the listed generalization-gap predictors in the tested competition setting.

record.problems: The reported results are primarily correlations across model collections, not causal tests; uncertainty intervals are not reported. ImageNet training accuracy remains predictive, and the authors identify transformation suitability and extension beyond image data as limitations.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the many single-transformation, paired-transformation, and individual RandAugment N/M correlation results from Sections 4.3 and 4.4; they are extensive and address the proposed estimator's ablations rather than a claim version. The main aggregate and condition-sensitive results are retained.

untested.parts: Joint random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level random-label test accuracy under the specified recipes.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and their test-error trends.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers, local connectivity, and initialization effects.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Isolated batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptation of the training recipe.
Dropout interventions, small-data and underfitting regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.

Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Table 4 does not specify the sharpness variant or provide these comparisons.
Removal of examples selected by memorization influence versus equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The rows describe estimator evaluation and its baselines, so they should not be treated as evidence rows for V1–V8. Their cannot_determine states concern those versions, not whether the reported correlations exist. Table 4 is outside the versions because its sharpness measure is unspecified and its comparison reports predictor performance. No version-relevant missing result was identified.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and test performance on natural labels.
Width beyond interpolation and test-error trends.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes.
Effects of dropout and its removal.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
